::: {#def-taylor-polynomial}
#### Taylor polynomial and Taylor series

Let $f$ be a function that has at least $n$ derivatives at a point $x_0$.
The **Taylor polynomial** of degree $n$ for $f$ centered at $x_0$ is:

$$
\begin{aligned}
P_n(x)
&= \sum_{k=0}^n \frac{f^{(k)}(x_0)}{k!}(x - x_0)^k \\
&= f(x_0) + f'(x_0)(x - x_0) + \frac{f''(x_0)}{2!}(x - x_0)^2 + \dots + \frac{f^{(n)}(x_0)}{n!}(x - x_0)^n
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-taylor-poly-def}

When $x_0 = 0$, $P_n(x)$ is called the **Maclaurin polynomial**.
When $f$ is infinitely differentiable and the series converges to $f(x)$ on an open interval containing $x_0$, the infinite sum $\sum_{k=0}^\infty \frac{f^{(k)}(x_0)}{k!}(x - x_0)^k$ is the **Taylor series** of $f$ centered at $x_0$.
:::
